newsitem.title: USA: Walter Mondale rejoins Minneapolis law firm.
newsitem.headline: Walter Mondale rejoins Minneapolis law firm.

text.p: Former Vice President Walter Mondale, who resigned last month as U.S. ambassador to Japan, said on Sunday he has rejoined a Minneapolis-based law firm to focus on international business.

Mondale, who turned 69 on Sunday, said he was very pleased to rejoin the law firm of Dorsey & Whitney LLP, which has 400 attorneys worldwide and where he was a partner prior to becoming ambassador to Japan in 1993.

"We are living in a dynamic global economy," Mondale said in a statement. "American companies are leading the way. Dorsey & Whitney represents a wide range of clients -- from Fortune 500 companies to emerging high-tech firms -- that are expanding throughout the world. I hope I can be of some help."

Mondale, who served as vice president under Jimmy Carter and was the Democratic nominee for president in 1984, also said he expected to remain active in civic and education affairs at the local, national and international levels.
